what: Cross-book claim that Python and JavaScript translate one sentence at a time, every time it is read, is wrong: CPython compiles the whole file to bytecode before running, and JS engines compile/JIT. It also contradicts the Python book (see INTEGRATION_TODO 'CROSS-BOOK CLAIM', same mistake as rust ch1 P5).
evidence: Panel 6 INTERPRETED card: "An interpreter sits beside you and translates one sentence at a time, every time you read it. Easy to start, but slower. Python and JavaScript usually run like this." Words page: "compiled / interpreted: Translated once, before running (C++) / translated while running (Python, usually)."
fix: Change the card to "An interpreter translates and runs the program each time you start it, so there's no separate build step. Python and JavaScript usually work like this." and the Words entry to "/ translated each time it runs, with no separate build step (Python, usually)".

what: The stated reason for g++ 13's 202100 is doubtful. GCC 13.1 came out in April 2023, after the C++23 technical work was finished (Feb 2023). As far as I can tell, the 202302L value only went into GCC 14 (a June 2023 commit, which I couldn't open: sourceware returned a bot block). Treat the claim as unverified.
evidence: Machine note: "g++ 13 was built before C++23 was finished, so it reports a placeholder number, 202100." Notebook: "the number was not final when that compiler was released." Scratch run: g++ 13.3 also prints 202100 for -std=gnu++23 and -std=c++2b.
fix: Machine note: "g++ 13 still uses a placeholder number for C++23, 202100. Newer compilers say 202302." Notebook: "g++ 13's 202100 is a placeholder that this version never updated."

what: The page tells readers that linker errors have no file address and that 'a file address means the Compiler'. The captured linker message on the same panel does contain a file:line address, because -g adds debug info.
evidence: add_missing.cpp capture: "/usr/bin/ld: add_missing.o: in function `main':\n/home/you/cpp-ch2/add_missing.cpp:6:(.text+0x13): undefined reference to `add(int, int)'". Map note: "A linker error: no file address, no caret, no program." ex-label why: "Compiler errors start with file:line:col: and show a caret. This one has neither." Recap: "A file address: the Compiler."
fix: Map note: "A linker error: no column, no caret, no program." ex-label why: "Compiler errors start with file:line:col: and show a caret. This one comes from /usr/bin/ld and has no column or caret (the add_missing.cpp:6 it mentions is where add was called)." Recap: "`file:line:col: error:` is the Compiler; `/usr/bin/ld` is the linker". In the Linker bubble, add one sentence explaining the :6.

what: Over-general claim, contradicted by the clang++ terminal shown next to it: fatal errors do not always come alone. clang++ reports earlier errors before a missing header, and its own report here ends with an error count.
evidence: Wren: "No other line was even checked. Fatal errors always come alone." Scratch test (fatal2.cpp: `int x = ;` on line 3, `#include <nosuch>` on line 5): clang++ 18 printed "fatal2.cpp:3:13: error: expected expression" then "fatal error: 'nosuch' file not found", "2 errors generated." (g++ 13 printed only the fatal error.)
fix: "The preprocessor couldn't find a drawer called iostrem, so it stopped dead: compilation terminated. Nothing after that line gets checked."

what: Slightly inaccurate: std::cerr is unit-buffered (it flushes after every output operation), not 'not buffered at all'.
evidence: "std::cerr, the error stream, is not buffered at all." cppreference std::cerr: unitbuf is set, so output is flushed after each operation.
fix: "std::cerr, the error stream, ships every piece of output immediately."

what: The lab instruction predicts a result that doesn't happen with the book's build command: -Wextra also turns on -Wuninitialized, so removing only -Wall still prints the warning.
evidence: Lab: "Build uninit.cpp with and without -Wall. The warning only appears with it." Scratch: `g++ -std=c++23 -Wextra -g uninit.cpp` still prints "warning: 'score' is used uninitialized [-Wuninitialized]". With no warning flags at all, it prints nothing.
fix: "Build uninit.cpp with and without -Wall -Wextra. The warning only appears with them."
